correctness.rationale: For lambda>0 the proposed profile is continuous, has U'=−lambda(1−U) behind the interface, and takes every value in (0,1) there. Dividing the traveling-wave equation by 1−U gives a polynomial with coefficients lambda²−c lambda, (2 beta−2)lambda²+lambda+1, and −3 beta lambda²+k lambda. Vanishing identically is equivalent to c=lambda, 2(1−beta)lambda²=lambda+1 and k=3 beta lambda. The positive root is unique for 0<beta<1, with the stated formula, and impossible at beta=1 or above. On the zero side the equation is satisfied; the profile and the flux D(U)U'−h(U) have matching traces across the interface because D(0)=0 and h is continuous. Thus no delta mass appears and the matching is sufficient distributionally. For example beta=5/8 yields c=2 and k=15/4 by the same coefficient equations. This proves the iff only within the specified profile family; it does not establish an all-profile minimal speed or stability theorem. The frozen algebra script was inspected rather than executed.

value.rationale: Although coefficient matching is routine once the ansatz is chosen, the curve provides an exact, nontrivial weak sharp-front benchmark in the positive two-parameter model for which prior work investigates the speed and profile numerically. It links deformation of the diffusion and nonlinear convection to an explicit profile and propagation speed and determines exactly when the canonical exponential ansatz works, rather than exhibiting a fortuitous numerical parameter. This is useful for comparison with phase-plane or numerical wave predictions; it is not a general wave-speed classification.
